While the story is very atmospheric and well-written, it relies on familiar, classic tropes of grief, memory, and gothic mystery (such as returning to an abandoned childhood home after decades, seeing one's deceased parent in the mirror, finding a faded mysterious note, and smelling a lingering, impossible scent). Because it ends on a cliffhanger just as the mystery is introduced, it serves more as a mood piece than an exploration of a unique or original idea that would offer the reader a new perspective or deeper understanding of human nature.
